To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have presented an algorithm for the maximum sum segment and the maximum density segment problems that runs faster than the existing algorithms; 2) we have presented a simple geometric algorithm for the maximum density segment problem; and 3) we have presented algorithms for the problems of length-constrained heaviest segments.
We present an algorithm for length-constrained heavey segments problems with time and space complexity in  O(n).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the maximum sum or maximum density segment of a given sequence of real numbers with a given length constraint.
the problems of finding length-constrainted heaviest segments in sequences of real numbers.
the problems of finding the maximum sum segment and the maximum density segment for a sequence of n numbers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown the following: (a) For the first problem there is a simple and elegant algorithm with time complexity O(n), space complexity O(U).

the problem of length-constrained heaviest segment is solvable in linear time for any given width and the problem of length constrained maximum density segment is solvable with the same time complexity in O(1) space for any given uniform width and in O(n) space for any uniform or non-uniform width.
the problem of finding heaviest segments for a sequence of n numbers with length constraints L <= U is solvable in O(n) time and O(U) space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we give a new algorithm for the length-constrained maximum density segment problem and improve the time complexities of the algorithms for the problems of length-constrained maximum and minimum sum segment problems.
we have presented efficient algorithms for length-constraint heaviest segment problems.

we give algorithms with time complexity O(n) and with space complexity O(U) for the problems of length-constrained maximum and maximum density segment for a sequence of n numbers with arbitrary real values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometric algorithms are more efficient than the combinatorial ones.
we can solve these two problems with the same algorithm.
the problem of finding the heaviest segment of a given length can be reduced to the problem of finding a segment whose density is the maximum.
